source.title: A meta-analytic investigation of the antecedents, theoretical correlates, and consequences of moral disengagement at work

confidence_rationale: The only entry in this directory operating at genuine ORGANIZATIONAL scale, which is the scale MECH-012 is actually about, and a meta-analysis in the field's leading journal. Scored mixed and held at 0.60 for two reasons. First, the evidence base is self-report scales measuring a disposition to disengage, not a manipulated symbolic channel, so causal direction and the role of language are both inferred rather than shown. Second, one of its headline results cuts against a strong reading of the claim: moral disengagement predicted HIGHER guilt and shame after misconduct. I could not access full text and have quoted no effect sizes or k/N figures.
failure_signatures: Moral disengagement was POSITIVELY related to guilt and shame POST-misconduct while reducing moral awareness, moral judgment and ANTICIPATED guilt beforehand. An REE model in which institutional absorption deletes or discharges residue predicts the opposite. What is suppressed is the PROSPECTIVE gating function of residue, not the residue itself -- which survives and re-presents after the act.

The contextual effects are ASYMMETRIC: abusive supervision and organizational politics were strong ENABLERS while ethical leadership and organizational justice were relatively weak DETERRENTS. A REE mitigation strategy built on adding virtuous institutional language is therefore predicted to be weak relative to removing the enabling conditions -- the channel is easier to use for denial than for absorption at organizational scale, which is the reverse of the symmetry Bandura et al. 1975 found in the laboratory.

Moral disengagement showed incremental validity over narcissism, Machiavellianism, psychopathy and entitlement. The mechanism is therefore not reducible to selecting bad actors into institutions -- which closes off the easiest alternative explanation for institutional harm and leaves MECH-012's structural account standing.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A meta-analytic review of moral disengagement at work -- the cognitive tactics by which people sidestep the moral self-regulatory processes that normally prevent wrongdoing. Abusive supervision and perceived organizational politics emerged as strong contextual enablers, while ethical leadership and organizational justice were relatively weak deterrents. Moral disengagement was positively associated with workplace misconduct and turnover intentions and negatively with organizational citizenship behaviours and task performance, with the effect on misconduct mediated by lower moral awareness, lower moral judgment and lower anticipated guilt. It retained incremental validity over the dark-triad traits and psychological entitlement. Contrary to a strong disengagement account, it was positively related to guilt and shame AFTER misconduct.
mapping.ree_translation: Bandura's disengagement tactics are the operational inventory of MECH-012's institutional repertoire: euphemistic labelling and moral justification are denial, displacement of responsibility is absorption, diffusion of responsibility is diffusion, and dehumanization is the removal of the target's standing to generate residue. This meta-analysis establishes that the repertoire predicts misconduct at organizational scale and is enabled by organizational conditions rather than reducible to individual pathology. Its most valuable contribution to REE, though, is a correction. The mediation runs through ANTICIPATED guilt, moral awareness and moral judgment -- the prospective, gating uses of the moral signal -- while post-hoc guilt and shame went UP. Read into REE: institutions do not delete residue, they sever its control pathway. The marker is still written; it simply no longer participates in the decision that would have prevented the harm, and it re-presents afterwards with nowhere to go. That is a far better account of institutional moral injury than 'the residue was absorbed', and it implies a specific REE architecture: residue write and residue-to-policy gating must be separable, because the evidence says institutions attack the second while leaving the first intact.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a meta-analysis of predominantly cross-sectional self-report studies. Moral disengagement is measured as a propensity on a questionnaire, not as an institutional utterance manipulated by the experimenter, so the LANGUAGE clause of MECH-012 is inferred from Bandura's theoretical taxonomy rather than tested; causal direction between disengagement and misconduct is not established by these designs. The outcome is workplace misconduct as rated or self-reported, not embodied harm. I could not access the full text (paywalled at both publisher and aggregator) and have therefore recorded no effect sizes, no k, and no total N -- every statement above is drawn from the abstract, which I read verbatim via PubMed. Anyone relying on magnitudes should obtain the article.
mapping.source_context: Meta-analysis of workplace/organizational studies of moral disengagement in adult employees; predominantly self-report survey designs; outcomes include misconduct, citizenship behaviours, turnover intentions and task performance.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality is high (leading journal, cumulative evidence, incremental validity tested against competing trait accounts) and mapping_fidelity is the binding constraint: self-reported disengagement propensity is several inferential steps from 'institutional language displaces residue'. The aggregate sits nearer mapping_fidelity than source_quality because MECH-012 is a mechanism hypothesis, where fidelity is what governance needs.
